questions.question: How do you manage configuration for a Go service across environments (dev/staging/prod)?
questions.title: Environment Config Go
questions.direct_answer: 12-factor: config in env vars, the app reads via os.Getenv/LookupEnv at startup. The same binary everywhere; the env vars differ. Structs with defaults, validation, and fail-fast on missing.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    DEV[.env file] --> S[os.Setenv at init]
    DOCK[docker -e] --> E[process environment]
    K8S[configMap + secret] --> E
    E --> G[os.Getenv at startup]
    G --> C[Config struct — validated]
    C --> F[fail fast on missing]
    C --> APP[dependencies + server — pass struct]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The config-loading lifecycle (the startup discipline): main loads config → validates → constructs dependencies (the DB pool from the DSN) → starts the server. The fail-fast contract: a missing required variable errors at STARTUP (in one place, with a clear message) — never mid-request in a deep goroutine. The anti-pattern the question catches: os.Getenv scattered through the codebase (config read at request time = a config change needs no restart = an inconsistent-config bug).

The typed-config pattern (the next step): parse the env into a typed struct once; pass the struct (or its fields) everywhere. The code below the config layer NEVER touches os.Getenv — the config's single load point is the seam that makes it testable (inject a different Config) and auditable (one place lists every knob).

The secrets layer: env vars are readable via docker inspect / the process environment — for actual secrets (DB passwords, API keys), Kubernetes secrets or a vault beat plain env vars. The 12-factor rule's production refinement: config in env, secrets in the secret manager, mounted as env at container start.
